text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- State-owned airline Air Malta expects to report a loss for the financial year to the end of March, chief executive Louis Grech said. It would be the first time the airline reported a loss since 1975. Air Malta lost $10 million from core operations last year but shortfall was made up by profits from subsidiaries and extraordinary revenue. The decline has been attributed to excess capacity as the airline opened new routes to promote Malta as an airline hub. The purchase of three regional airliners has also been criticized in an internal airline report.
- Maltese working in Albania on voluntary aid projects including the building of churches and schools, are safe.
- Police find heroin valued at $1 million in raid on apartment. Several Maltese and Libyans were arrested, but one Libyan is still being hunted.

- Opposition Nationalist Party leader Eddie Fenech Adami stresses emphasis on looking after the people in speech to rally ahead of next Saturday's council elections in a third of Malta's towns and villages.
